drills.q: State the five-phase timebox for one 20-minute coding problem.
drills.a: 0-2min restate/clarify, 2-4min state target complexity, 4-14min write while narrating, 14-17min trace 2-3 named test cases, 17-20min state final complexity and take the follow-up trap.

drills.q: Name the three test cases you should trace unprompted after any solution.
drills.a: Happy path, empty/single-element edge case, and one pattern-specific adversarial case (duplicates, already-sorted, negatives).

drills.q: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters -- what pattern, and what's the key optimization over a naive sliding window?
drills.a: Sliding window with a hash map of last-seen index. The optimization: jump the left pointer directly to last_seen[char]+1 instead of shrinking one character at a time, keeping it O(n) instead of O(n^2).

drills.q: Meeting Rooms II: what data structure and why, and what wrong pattern do candidates reach for instead?
drills.a: Min-heap of end times (push each meeting's end, pop when current start >= heap top) -- it's a max-concurrent-intervals problem. Candidates wrongly reach for Merge Intervals logic, which answers 'does anything overlap,' a different question.

drills.q: Course Schedule: what's the algorithm, and what's the one-line extension to return an actual valid order instead of yes/no?
drills.a: Kahn's BFS topological sort using in-degree counts; completable iff all nodes dequeue. Extension: the dequeue order itself IS a valid course order -- trivial for Kahn's, but exposes candidates who only memorized the boolean version.

drills.q: Top K Frequent Elements: name two O(n)-or-better approaches and the tradeoff between them.
drills.a: Min-heap of size k (O(n log k), generalizes to streaming) or bucket sort by frequency (O(n), since frequency is bounded by array length, but doesn't generalize to an infinite stream needing a running top-k).

drills.q: Alien Dictionary: what's the specific invalid-input case most candidates miss?
drills.a: A shorter word appearing AFTER a longer word that has it as a prefix (e.g. ['abc','ab']) -- there's no valid ordering, and candidates who compare full words character-by-character instead of stopping at the first difference miss this case.

drills.q: Word Search II: what data structure should be built first, and why does it beat running DFS per dictionary word?
drills.a: A Trie built from the whole dictionary first, then one shared DFS from every grid cell following Trie edges with pruning. Beats per-word DFS because it shares the traversal cost across all words instead of paying O(words x grid) independently.

drills.q: Dropout question analog for coding: your traced test case fails with 8 minutes left. What's the WRONG move and the RIGHT move?
drills.a: Wrong: rewrite the solution from scratch. Right: state the symptom before touching code, isolate the smallest fix, and if time runs out, name the bug and believed fix explicitly rather than claiming it's done.

drills.q: What makes a coding-round answer score a 4-5 on 'Seniority signals' rather than a 3?
drills.a: Unprompted: naming and rejecting an alternative approach with a reason ('brute force is O(n^2), rejecting because n can be 10^5'), diagnosing a failing test's symptom before touching code, and asking about input size/mutability before assuming them.

drills.q: What's the NO HIRE band (5-8/20) defined by in the coding round rubric?
drills.a: One problem correct, the other wrong or abandoned; complexity claims wrong and undefended; long silent stretches; no unprompted edge-case handling.
